Tripathi is a 'deep, slow' baritone, yet his lines run 9.3 to 9.6 (l23, l31, l32). l12 fits a [laughs] into 2.8 s. I hand-counted the characters in the Gate 0b v4 Hindi takes (content/proof/photoreal/voice/manifest.jsonl and content/proof/flat2d/voice/manifest.jsonl, clip durations) and got about 8.4 and 8.9 chars/s. On that basis the stated 128.7 s is about 136 s before the staging time in item 2 is added. Fix: (a) Re-target l14 4.9, l15 2.8, l17 3.5, l19 5.8, l21 4.1, l22 4.0, l24 3.8, l25 4.5, l23 2.8, l31 3.3, l32 5.6, l12 3.4 (+7.7 s). (b) Pay for that and for item 2 (+2.1 s). Trim l13 to '[calm] नक़ली Inspector पकड़ा है। ले जाइए।' at 3.9 s (l03's confession already states the theft): -1.5 s. Cut b3 silent_seconds from 2.0 to 1.6 and b5 from 1.5 to 1.2: -0.7 s. (c) Recompute target_total_seconds. By my arithmetic that gives about 134.7 s, 31 lines and about 978 characters. If you would rather keep l04, cut l10 instead and give Bhaiyaji's smile still 0.6 s of b4's silence.

STILLS-ONLY STAGING (must fix): four beats have shots with no time, so the edit will either drop them or add the time. In b6, three look stills plus the pad insert share 1.5 s of silence (about 0.4 s each), and Shot 8 (Nirala understands, 'No line on it') gets 0 s, though the bible makes that face the beat's payoff. In b8, four inserts share 1.2 s after l22, and the last of them, Bhaiyaji's eyes on the phone, is what l30 later rests on. b10 Shot 2 (the key-ring insert between l26 and l27, same speaker, no gap) has no line and no silence. Neither does b11 Shot 1 (Bhaiyaji sits, the smile gone for the first time in the series). Fixes: b6, set silent_seconds to 2.4 before, over three stills: Nirala on his sack; the scale with the revolver in the foreground and the loaded truck behind it (one still covers the bible's truck and revolver); the pad and pen-click insert. Keep l14 over Shot 5, play l16 over Shot 8 (Nirala's hands coming off his knees) and drop Shot 7. b8, set silent_seconds to 2.4 after, over three inserts of about 0.8 s each: the key coming out of the cab door, her hand lifting the phone off the sack, Bhaiyaji's eyes on it. Drop the pocket insert and let the sfx clink carry it. b10, move the key-ring insert into the 0.8 s line pause before l29, as the room's reaction to 'Force भेजिए।', and play l26 and l27 over two framings of Nandini so the cut between them still separates the takes. b11, merge Shots 1 and 2 into one two-shot: Bhaiyaji seated on a sack picture-left, smile gone, nodding at the phone, with Tripathi standing picture-right looking down at him, l30 over it. Net cost +2.1 s, already counted in the LENGTH item.

CONTINUITY (must fix): from b10 her hands hold more than two hands can, and the memo pad, the episode's central prop, disappears. She holds the pad and pen from b6 and the phone as well from b8. She dials with the phone at her ear in b10 and takes the revolver in b11. b12 Shot 3 then reads 'the revolver in one hand and the phone in the other; her hand goes to the buttoned left chest pocket', and the pad and pen are never put down. Under D-013 rule 3 this state is copied into every frame prompt, and b12 Shot 3 is the cliffhanger hold. That front-on close also does not say how the revolver is held, and the bible rule is 'held in profile, never pointed at a face or at the camera'. Fix: in b10 Shot 1, add 'before dialling she slides the memo pad into her right trouser pocket and clips the pen back in her left chest pocket'. Rewrite b12 Shot 3 as 'close, Nandini, front on: the wooden revolver in her right hand at her side, barrel to the floor, in profile (or out of frame); her left hand, still holding the phone, comes to rest flat over the buttoned left chest pocket where the medal is. Hold.' Update the props paragraph in writer_notes to match.

LENGTH (series-level, for the orchestrator and Arbiter, not the writer): at the measured pace of about 8.7 chars/s, D-016's 1,050-character measure is about 120 s of speech on its own, so no Series 2 episode written to it can finish near the 120 s target.
